results.question: Who can get the general social security benefit when they are unemployed?

results.question: Is there a waiting period before I can get the general social security benefit?
results.answer: You can get the general social security benefit after you have been registered as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services for at least 7 working days [S2]. This is called a waiting period [S2]. You cannot get the general social security benefit during the waiting period [S2]. You only have to complete one waiting period for the general social security benefit [S2]. You do not need to complete a waiting period of 7 working days if you go directly from earnings-related unemployment allowance to the general social security benefit [S5]. The periodisation of your holiday compensation will not apply at the same time as your waiting period [S8].

results.question: I have no vocational qualification. Do I have to wait longer before I get the general social security benefit?
results.answer:
If you do not have a vocational qualification or a higher education degree, you must complete a qualifying period (odotusaika) before you can receive the general social security benefit [S1][S4]. 

The maximum length of this qualifying period is 21 weeks, which is about 5 months [S3][S8]. Upper secondary school education (lukio) or the matriculation examination is not considered a vocational qualification [S1][S4]. Furthermore, if you are under 25, you must also apply for admission to at least two study programmes starting in the autumn term to qualify for the benefit [S4][S8].

results.question: How does part-time work affect my general social security benefit?
results.answer:

results.question: Can income other than wages reduce my general social security benefit?
results.answer:
Yes, other types of income besides wages or salary can reduce your general social security benefit [S1][S3]. Kela takes income like capital income, informal care allowances, partial early old-age pensions, compensations for family caregivers, and copyright royalties into account in means testing [S2][S3]. 

You can have up to EUR 311 per month in capital income or other non-wage income without it affecting your benefit [S4]. If this income exceeds EUR 311 per month, 50% of the amount exceeding the limit will be deducted from your benefit [S4]. However, if you participate in employment-promoting services, non-wage income will not reduce your general social security benefit [S4]. Savings, assets, and the income of a partner or roommate do not affect the benefit [S3].
